statements.label: supported
statements.text: When human populations were compared, higher rates of horizontal gene transfer among gut bacteria went together with industrialized lifestyles.
statements.evidence: Comparison across human populations reveals that industrialized lifestyles are associated with higher HGT rates
statements.note: The abstract states that, across the compared populations, industrialized lifestyles are associated with higher HGT rates.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Horizontal gene transfers have built up in the human gut microbiome over recent generations of hosts.
statements.evidence: We show that HGTs have accumulated in the microbiome over recent host generations
statements.note: The abstract reports that HGTs accumulated in the microbiome over recent host generations.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Antibiotic use in industrialized populations is what raises the rate of horizontal gene transfer among their gut bacteria.
statements.evidence: Our results suggest that gut bacteria continuously acquire new functionality based on host lifestyle and that high rates of HGT may be a recent development in human history linked to industrialization.
statements.note: The abstract ties higher HGT rates to industrialized lifestyles in general but never mentions antibiotics or names any specific cause.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The horizontal gene transfer analysis covered thousands of bacterial strains drawn from 15 human populations that differ in their degree of industrialization.
statements.evidence: thousands of bacterial strains from 15 human populations spanning a range of industrialization
statements.note: The abstract describes examining HGT across thousands of strains from 15 populations spanning a range of industrialization.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The ethylene-dependent ripening circuits arose more often through neofunctionalisation than through repurposing of pre-existing genes.
statements.evidence: These circuits are evolved from senescence or floral organ identity pathways in the ancestral angiosperms either by neofunctionalisation or repurposing pre-existing genes.
statements.note: The abstract names both routes of origin but gives no indication of which one was more frequent.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In dry fruits and in fleshy fruits that ripen independently of ethylene, H3K27me3 plays a conserved role in restraining ripening genes and their orthologues.
statements.evidence: The epigenome, H3K27me3 in particular, has played a conserved role in restricting ripening genes and their orthologues in dry and ethylene-independent fleshy fruits.
statements.note: The abstract states that H3K27me3 has had a conserved role in restricting ripening genes and their orthologues in dry and ethylene-independent fleshy fruits.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Fruit ripening that depends on ethylene is governed by three kinds of transcriptional feedback circuit, identified from fruitENCODE data including 361 transcriptome and 45 DNA methylation profiles.
statements.evidence: Analysis of the fruitENCODE data consisting of 361 transcriptome, 71 accessible chromatin, 147 histone and 45 DNA methylation profiles reveals three types of transcriptional feedback circuits controlling ethylene-dependent fruit ripening.
statements.note: Analysis of fruitENCODE data, which included 361 transcriptome and 45 DNA methylation profiles, revealed three types of feedback circuits controlling ethylene-dependent ripening.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The ethylene-dependent ripening circuits trace back to senescence or floral organ identity pathways that existed in ancestral angiosperms.
statements.evidence: These circuits are evolved from senescence or floral organ identity pathways in the ancestral angiosperms
statements.note: The abstract states that the ripening circuits evolved from senescence or floral organ identity pathways of ancestral angiosperms.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Most whole-genome duplications reported in earlier work were confirmed, and strong evidence emerged for previously unknown ones in many angiosperm lineages.
statements.evidence: These analyses confirmed most of the previously reported WGDs and provided strong evidence for novel ones in many lineages.
statements.note: The abstract reports confirmation of most previously reported WGDs plus strong evidence for novel WGDs in many lineages.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Data from the detected whole-genome duplications support an exponential model of gene loss, with an estimated half-life of about 21.6 million years.
statements.evidence: The detected WGDs supported a model of exponential gene loss during evolution with an estimated half-life of approximately 21.6 million years
statements.note: The abstract states that the detected WGDs supported exponential gene loss with an estimated half-life of approximately 21.6 million years.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Gene functions belonging to essential cellular metabolism showed preferential retention in the angiosperm genomes and transcriptomes analysed.
statements.evidence: uncovered preferential retention of gene functions in essential cellular metabolisms
statements.note: The abstract reports that the analyses uncovered preferential retention of gene functions in essential cellular metabolism.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Whole-genome duplications occurred more often in angiosperms than in gymnosperms or ferns.
statements.evidence: We performed comparative genomic and phylogenomic analyses of 59 public genomes/transcriptomes and 46 newly sequenced transcriptomes covering major lineages of angiosperms
statements.note: The sampled genomes and transcriptomes are described as covering angiosperm lineages, and no comparison with gymnosperms or ferns is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genes found in only a subset of Brachypodium distachyon lines show faster rates of evolution and lie nearer to transposable elements.
statements.evidence: genes present in only some lines are enriched for conditionally beneficial functions (e.g., defense and development), display faster evolutionary rates, lie closer to transposable elements
statements.note: The abstract states that genes present in only some lines display faster evolutionary rates and lie closer to transposable elements.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Brachypodium distachyon genes present in only some lines are expressed at lower levels than genes present in all lines.
statements.evidence: genes present in only some lines are enriched for conditionally beneficial functions (e.g., defense and development), display faster evolutionary rates, lie closer to transposable elements and are less likely to be syntenic with orthologous genes in other grasses
statements.note: The abstract describes function, evolutionary rate, proximity to transposable elements and synteny for these genes but reports nothing about their expression levels.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A pan-genome built from 54 de novo assembled Brachypodium distachyon lines contains almost double the genes present in any single genome.
statements.evidence: Whole-genome de novo assembly and annotation of 54 lines of the grass Brachypodium distachyon yield a pan-genome containing nearly twice the number of genes found in any individual genome.
statements.note: The abstract states that the 54-line pan-genome contains nearly twice the number of genes found in any individual genome.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Essential biological functions are overrepresented among the Brachypodium distachyon genes that every line carries.
statements.evidence: Genes present in all lines are enriched for essential biological functions
statements.note: The abstract states that genes present in all lines are enriched for essential biological functions.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Similar within-species mtDNA diversity across animal phyla results from mtDNA per-generation mutation rate being negatively correlated with effective population size.
statements.evidence: the among-phyla homogeneity in within-species mtDNA diversity is due to a negative correlation between mtDNA per-generation mutation rate and effective population size
statements.note: The abstract attributes the among-phyla homogeneity in mtDNA diversity to a negative correlation between per-generation mtDNA mutation rate and effective population size.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Vertebrates such as birds and scaled reptiles show a much higher mtDNA-to-nuDNA mutation rate ratio, above 20 on average, than insects and arachnids, at 2 to 6.
statements.evidence: In nonvertebrates, such as insects and arachnids, the ratio of mtDNA over nuDNA mutation rate varies between 2 and 6, whereas it is above 20, on average, in vertebrates such as scaled reptiles and birds.
statements.note: The abstract gives a ratio of 2 to 6 for nonvertebrates such as insects and arachnids versus above 20 on average for vertebrates such as scaled reptiles and birds.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Birds have a higher absolute per-year mitochondrial DNA mutation rate than insects.
statements.evidence: Finally, we explore the variation in the absolute per-year mutation rate of both mtDNA and nuDNA using a reduced data set for which fossil calibration is available
statements.note: The abstract says per-year rates were explored in a fossil-calibrated subset but reports no per-year values or any bird-insect comparison.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The mitochondrial-to-nuclear mutation rate ratio differs greatly among animal taxa, based on data sets covering 4,676 species.
statements.evidence: Analyzing 121 multilocus data sets and four phylogenomic data sets encompassing 4,676 species of animals, we demonstrate that the ratio of mitochondrial over nuclear mutation rate is highly variable among animal taxa.
statements.note: The abstract reports that, across data sets covering 4,676 animal species, the mitochondrial over nuclear mutation rate ratio is highly variable among taxa.
